text: Working with APIs is a common task for developers. An API allows your program to communicate with another service by sending HTTP requests. Most APIs return data in JSON format, which is easy to read and use. Before you can access an API, you often need authentication, such as an API key, to prove who you are. APIs also have rate limits, which means you can only send a certain number of requests within a period. Finally, good error handling is important. If a request fails, your program should check the status code and respond properly instead of crashing.
